Empirical Research Plan  
“Control Rights and Capital Structure: Evidence from Covenant Violations”

----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------------------
Primary strategy: Difference-in-Differences with staggered treatment (DiD-FE), complemented by an event-study / local RD robustness check.

Why DiD?  
• Covenant violations generate a discrete, externally-imposed transfer of control rights from shareholders to creditors.  
• Violations are (largely) unforeseen ex ante and unrelated to contemporaneous leverage choices, satisfying the exogeneity requirement.  
• We observe firms both before and after the violation as well as a panel of firms that never violate (or not yet), permitting a before–after, treated–control comparison with firm and time fixed effects.  
• The “parallel-trend” assumption can be tested in pre-violation periods.

Why not rely solely on RD?  
The continuous distance-to-covenant variable is noisily measured and violations sometimes occur by waiver or renegotiation, so the threshold is “fuzzy.” RD is therefore reserved for robustness to support the DiD findings.

----------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 for all firm-quarters (or firm-years) beginning with the fiscal period in which the firm first violates at least one financial covenant in an outstanding loan.

Control group (counterfactual)  
(i) Firms that have outstanding covenants but have not (yet) violated by that calendar year/quarter;  
(ii) For within-firm identification we implicitly use the same firm in pre-violation periods.

Treatment timing / variation  
• Event time τ = 0 is the first fiscal period containing the violation.  
• We code dynamic leads/lags τ = –8,…,–1,0,1,…,8 (two years if quarterly, eight years if annual).  
• When a firm violates again later, τ is reset only once (first violation) and subsequent violations are ignored or coded with separate dummies in robustness checks.

----------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of violation, leverage of would-be violators would follow the same trend as never-violating firms.  
• Plausibility: Covenant design often targets accounting ratios unrelated to leverage policy; pre-trends can be tested.

A2. No simultaneous shocks: No other event occuring exactly at τ = 0 differentially influences leverage for violators versus non-violators.  
• Plausibility: Violations sometimes coincide with negative performance shocks; we include firm×industry×time-varying controls and firm FE.

A3. Stable treatment: The change in control rights is homogeneous within treated firms; non-treated firms do not experience spillovers.  
• Plausibility: Control rights are contract specific; cross-firm spillovers unlikely.

A4. No anticipatory effects: Firms cannot perfectly foresee the violation far in advance and adjust leverage pre-emptively.  
• Plausibility: Technical violation is typically detected ex post by auditors/creditors; still, small anticipatory effects possible—tested via event-study pre-trends.

----------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
----------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Endogenous violation driven by declining performance that also drives leverage.  
  • Address with: (i) firm FE, calendar-time FE; (ii) control for performance variables (EBITDA, ROA); (iii) event-study to show flat pre-trends; (iv) IV/RD robustness using distance-to-covenant threshold.

T2. Sample attrition / survival bias (firms bankrupt after violation).  
  • Use inverse-probability weighting or joint modeling of exit; include bankrupt firms up to exit date; bound estimates (Lee bounds).

T3. Multiple treatment timing & staggered adoption bias (Goodman-Bacon).  
  • Estimate with sun-and-Abraham or Callaway-Sant’Anna estimators that purge negative weights; cluster at firm level.

----------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
----------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Required packages
library(data.table)     # fast data manipulation
library(fixest)         # high-dimensional FE regressions
library(did)            # Callaway-Sant’Anna DiD
library(ggplot2)

#------------------ 1. Load & merge data ----------------------
ds   <- fread("dealscan_loans_1990_2007.csv")
comp <- fread("compustat_1990_2007.csv")

# Merge by gvkey, fiscal year/quarter
setkey(ds, gvkey, fyearq)   # assume fyearq = yyyyq
setkey(comp, gvkey, fyearq)
panel <- merge(ds, comp, all.x = TRUE)

#------------------ 2. Construct variables --------------------
# Covenant violation dummy (from Dealscan flag)
panel[, viol := as.integer(covenant_violation == 1)]

# First violation date by gvkey
panel[, viol_first_q := fyearq[which(viol==1)[1]], by = gvkey]

# Treatment: post violation periods
panel[, treat := 0]
panel[!is.na(viol_first_q) & fyearq >= viol_first_q, treat := 1]

# Event-time variable
panel[, tau := fyearq - viol_first_q]

# Leverage ratio (book debt / assets)
panel[, lev := (dltt + dlc)/at]

# Control variables
panel[, log_assets := log(at)]
panel[, tangibility := ppent/at]
panel[, profitability := oibdp/at]

# Keep balanced window (optional)
panel_evt <- panel[tau >= -8 & tau <= 8]

#------------------ 3. Main DiD regression --------------------
# Two-way FE (firm & calendar-time), cluster by firm
did_main <- feols(lev ~ treat + log_assets + tangibility + profitability |
                  gvkey + fyearq, data = panel, cluster = ~gvkey)
summary(did_main)

#------------------ 4. Event-study ----------------------------
# Create leads/lags dummies
for(k in -8:8){
  if(k== -1 | k==0) next
  panel_evt[, paste0("tau",k) := as.integer(tau == k)]
}

formula_evt <- as.formula(
  paste("lev ~", paste(paste0("tau", -8:-2), collapse = " + "), " + ",
                     paste(paste0("tau",1:8), collapse = " + "),
                     "| gvkey + fyearq"))

evt <- feols(formula_evt, data = panel_evt, cluster = ~gvkey)
iplot(evt)   # visualize pre/post coefficients

#------------------ 5. Robustness: Fuzzy RD around threshold ---
# Assume variable dist = (Actual Ratio – Covenant Threshold)
panel_rd <- panel[abs(dist) <= 0.05]    # 5-ppt bandwidth
rd <- feols(lev ~ viol + dist | gvkey + fyearq, data = panel_rd,
            cluster = ~gvkey)
summary(rd)
```

----------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------------------
Theory predicts that when creditors obtain stronger control rights they curb risk-shifting and reduce leverage. Therefore:  
• Direction: Treated firms will lower leverage after a violation.  
• Magnitude: Prior papers show 2–3 p.p. decline in book leverage (~5–8 % of mean 40 % leverage) within two years.

----------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = yes, 0 = doubtful)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Well-defined treatment and timing ..................................... 1  
2. Parallel trends supported by pre-event data ........................... 1  
3. No major concurrent shocks / good controls ............................ 0.5  
4. Correct inference (clustering, staggered DiD issues handled) .......... 1  
5. External validity to wider population ................................. 0.5  
TOTAL (out of 5) ........................................................ 4.0
